summary: An employer's careers site: how the company works, what it offers, how hiring runs and who already works there, a searchable board of open roles, and a page per role with a validated application form.

pages.purpose: Help a candidate decide whether this is a place for them, and get them to the right open role.

sections.purpose: The employer promise in one line beside a list of teams with their open-role counts; choosing a team opens the board filtered to it.
sections.notes: A memorable version draws the teams on a dial with a needle that swings to the hovered team; the dial is decorative and the ruled team list is the accessible part (build from hero + list-layout). Choosing a team pre-sets the board filter.

sections.purpose: How the company works, as a few numbered principles beside a photo of the real workplace.
fields: Three to five working principles with title and sentence

sections.purpose: Open roles, locations, team size and other honest figures.
fields: Three or four figures with label and as-of date

sections.purpose: Every hiring stage with its typical duration and who the candidate meets.
fields: Stages with title, what happens and typical duration

sections.purpose: Short quotes from employees about their actual work.
sections.notes: Set as a ruled ledger of three quotes rather than avatar cards.

sections.purpose: The newest roles with a link to the full board.
sections.notes: Four newest roles as compact rows.

fields: Question and answer pairs (remote work, relocation, salary bands, feedback)

sections.purpose: For people with no matching role: send an open application or join a talent list.

pages.purpose: Every open role, searchable and filterable.

sections.purpose: Title, breadcrumb and the number of open roles.
Free-text search, team toggles, location and contract filters, a live result count, results grouped by team, and an empty state that offers to widen the search.
alternatives: data-table: very many roles with sortable columns
fields: Every role: reference, title, team, locations, contract type, salary band, posted date, closing date
sections.notes: The board is a role="search" region; the count is a status region. Search is case- and diacritic-insensitive. Filters survive a language switch. Each row is one link.

pages.purpose: One role in full, with the application form beside it.

sections.purpose: Breadcrumb, role title and a ruled fact strip.
What you will do, what you need, nice to have, and this role's hiring steps.
Apply for this role: name, email, CV upload, short note, location and right to work, plus consent for CV storage.
alternatives: multi-step-form: long applications with screening questions
fields: Consent text: what is stored, for how long, who sees it
sections.notes: Sticky column on wide screens. Validate on submit then on change; focus the first invalid field; end with a reference and a reply-by date. Consent checkbox must be unticked by default and state the retention period.

sections.purpose: Other roles in the same team.

content: Teams or departments with their open-role counts
Every open role: title, team, locations, contract type, salary band, posted and closing dates, responsibilities, requirements
Working principles or values with concrete examples
Benefits with concrete amounts or policies
Hiring stages, typical duration and who the candidate meets
Workplace photos of real people and places
Application rules: CV format and size, right-to-work requirement, screening questions
Candidate privacy notice: what is stored, retention period, who processes it
Reply-time promise and contact for questions

styles.name: calm and precise
styles.why: A tech or engineering employer: a Scandinavian-style grotesk with mono references, ruled ledgers instead of cards, calm entrance motion. Nothing showy for people deciding on a job.

styles.name: corporate employer
styles.why: A larger or more traditional employer whose careers site sits next to a corporate site and should look like the same company.

pitfalls: Discriminatory wording in job posts (age, gender, nationality) or asking for a photo, marital status or date of birth; many jurisdictions forbid it.
Collecting CVs without a candidate privacy notice, retention period and an unticked consent box.
Closed roles left on the board; every role needs a closing date and is removed after it.
No salary band: candidates skip roles without one, and some markets require it.
File upload without clear format and size limits, or errors shown only in colour.
Filter results and counts that change silently; announce them in a status region.
Stock photos of smiling strangers instead of real colleagues and workplaces.
